title: AminoTriComplex in Integrative Oncology: Integrated Preclinical Safety and Prospective Clinical Evidence in Metastatic Solid Tumors
content: Multi-component nutraceutical platforms are widely used in integrative oncology, yet standardized quality control, safety qualification, and biomarker-linked evidence remain limited. We integrated GMP manufacturing/QC data, GLP/OECD toxicology, an independent exploratory cancer-cell screening study, and prospective clinical evidence for AminoTriComplex across metastatic cancers. The in vitro screen evaluated coded AminoTriComplex (G1; 10 μg/mL for 48 hours) in 14 human cancer and non-tumor cell lines using a sulforhodamine B assay. Clinical datasets included a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC; n=72; 12 weeks) and controlled studies in stage IV lung adenocarcinoma (n=212; chemotherapy adjunct) and refractory triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC; n=266; metronomic backbone). Endpoints were RECIST v1.1 response, progression-free survival (PFS), CTCAE v5.0 safety, and a translational triad of Survivin, Cystatin C, and MT1/melatonin rhythm restoration. G1 produced the strongest broad viability reduction among four coded samples, although effects in HUVEC and BEAS-2B showed that tumor selectivity was not established. In mCRC, ORR was 53% versus 12% and median PFS 8.7 versus 3.2 months (HR 0.46). In lung adenocarcinoma, ORR was 48.7% versus 33.0% and DCR 78.3% versus 55.7%, without higher grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity. In TNBC, ORR was 46.3% versus 12.6% and median PFS 8.9 versus 3.4 months (HR 0.42), with concordant biomarker and tumor-microenvironment shifts. No signal of added serious clinical toxicity was observed. Final external preclinical safety assessments by Eurofins (Germany) and the Gamaleya National Research Center did not reveal mutagenic, genotoxic, embryotoxic, or carcinogenic potential under the tested conditions, and aged-rat experiments indicated enhanced mismatch-repair/DNA-repair activity. The non-selective single-dose cell-line signal nevertheless requires formal dose-response and selectivity studies. Trial registration: registry information should be inserted prior to submission; the mCRC trial was not prospectively registered.
